narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the status of your checking account, the total amount requested, and the length of the loan. Your checking account status was the most influential element and worked in your favor: having no checking account is relatively common among approved applicants (59%), and this profile pushed the prediction toward approval. Unfortunately, the other two major factors worked against you. You requested a loan of 10,366 DM, far above the average of about 3,020 DM seen among those who were approved. This large amount strongly increased the estimated risk. Similarly, a 60-month repayment period is more than three times the average duration of approved loans (19 months), which also pushed the decision noticeably toward denial.

Taken together, the substantially higher loan size and much longer repayment term outweighed the positive signal from your checking-account status, leading the model to classify you as too risky.

You should consider re-applying with a smaller loan amount and a shorter repayment period. Bringing your request closer to the averages that successful applicants typically show would likely improve your chances.
